subject: pathology
title: Renal cell carcinoma, Wilms and urothelial cancer

steps.tx: **Renal cell carcinoma** arises more often with smoking, obesity, hypertension and dialysis related acquired cystic disease in adults. Clear cell tumours lose **VHL** function and grow hypervascular, while papillary tumours associate with MET and chromophobe tumours carry the best prognosis overall. The classic triad of haematuria, flank pain and palpable mass now appears rarely because incidental imaging discovers most tumours earlier incidentally. Treatment uses partial or radical nephrectomy, while metastatic disease receives **targeted and immunotherapy** combinations in modern practice.
steps.say: Renal cell carcinoma is a tumour where clear cell histology predominates and VHL loss drives abnormal vascular growth signals inside cancer cells continuously during tumour expansion in kidneys of adults. Incidental detection occurs because imaging performed for other reasons discovers small renal masses before symptoms develop noticeably in many patients nowadays attending hospital investigations. Nephrectomy helps clinicians cure localised disease completely.

steps.tx: **Paraneoplastic syndromes** reveal renal cell carcinoma through hormones and mediators secreted by tumour cells into systemic circulation continuously. Ectopic erythropoietin causes polycythaemia, parathyroid hormone related protein causes hypercalcaemia, and renin secretion raises blood pressure in affected patients noticeably. **Stauffer syndrome** causes nonmetastatic hepatic dysfunction with raised alkaline phosphatase that resolves after nephrectomy removes the primary tumour successfully. New left varicocele or inferior vena cava thrombus warns that tumour extends into renal venous drainage locally.
steps.say: Paraneoplastic syndromes are clues where renal tumours secrete erythropoietin or hormone like mediators into blood and alter distant organ function measurably before metastases appear anywhere else in body scans. Varicocele development warns clinicians because tumour thrombus obstructs the left gonadal vein drainage into renal vein directly at its entry point anatomically. Resolution occurs because nephrectomy removes mediator source.

steps.tx: **Wilms tumour** is a nephroblastoma of toddlers that forms a triphasic tumour with blastemal, epithelial and stromal elements microscopically. Children present with a painless abdominal mass that feels large and may cross the midline on examination and imaging studies. Associations include **WAGR syndrome** with aniridia, Denys-Drash syndrome and Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome through WT1 and WT2 related mechanisms genetically. Chemotherapy with surgery cures most children, while **anaplasia** predicts worse behaviour and needs intensified treatment protocols.
steps.say: Wilms tumour is a childhood cancer where a painless abdominal mass grows large before parents notice abdominal swelling during bathing or dressing young toddlers at home routinely. Triphasic histology appears because blastemal cells mix with epithelial tubules and stromal elements under microscopy in classic nephroblastoma samples examined by pathologists. Chemotherapy helps clinicians cure most children nowadays.

steps.tx: This abdominal scan shows a huge left renal tumour expanding across the midline and compressing normal kidney into a thin **claw sign** rim. That intrarenal origin with midline extension in a young child points towards **Wilms tumour** rather than an adrenal neuroblastoma sitting above the kidney. The opposite kidney appears normal, which matters because bilateral disease changes surgical planning and renal preservation priorities in childhood cancer protocols. Examiners use this image because size, claw sign and midline crossing appear together.
steps.say: This scan shows a large renal tumour because the mass expands from kidney and compresses normal parenchyma into a claw shaped rim around its edge medially on imaging slices. Midline crossing occurs because the tumour grows huge before painless abdominal swelling brings toddlers to medical attention initially at hospital. Contralateral kidney assessment helps clinicians plan surgery safely.

steps.tx: **Urothelial carcinoma** follows smoking, aromatic amine dye exposure, cyclophosphamide and chronic schistosomal irritation of urinary tract epithelium over years. Patients present with **painless haematuria**, while flat carcinoma in situ behaves as high grade disease despite lacking a papillary mass endoscopically. Non muscle invasive tumours receive transurethral resection with intravesical **BCG therapy**, whereas muscle invasive disease requires cisplatin based chemotherapy and radical cystectomy for control. Upper tract tumours mirror bladder disease and usually require nephroureterectomy for definitive local treatment.
steps.say: Urothelial carcinoma is a cancer where smoking and dye exposure injure bladder epithelium over decades before malignant transformation becomes clinically apparent with haematuria episodes reported by older patients. Painless bleeding helps clinicians prioritise cystoscopy because infection and stones usually cause pain alongside urinary symptoms more often in routine practice settings. BCG therapy helps clinicians treat flat high grade disease.
